areas.name: Windows Route and Library Boundary
areas.location_cue: The EA app library, title screen, Packs panel, load menu, user-data folder, and installed-content filters.
areas.note: Chosen route: the current native Windows release with the owned first-party library, researched through July 18, 2026.

save_backup.title: Archive the user-data folder first
save_backup.why: World edits and household-state changes can be difficult to reverse cleanly.
save_backup.detail: Keep a dated, untouched copy outside the live game folder.

levels.1: The selected route uses the maintained PC edition and its modular content library.
levels.2: Install the current Windows build through the linked EA account and record its version.
levels.3: Launch online once, verify the base game and every owned add-on finishes downloading, record the build number and language, then open a test household to confirm the save and catalog load without missing-content warnings.

levels.1: New packs, Marketplace releases, patches, and events continue to change the available library.
levels.2: Treat this checklist as current through July 18, 2026.
levels.3: Before each completion audit, compare the installed add-on list with the current official store and Marketplace. Add later releases to a dated extension ledger instead of silently folding them into this cutoff.

levels.1: A full-library save contains irreversible deaths, household changes, and world edits.
levels.2: Copy the saves, tray, screenshots, and options folders before major experiments.
levels.3: Exit the game completely, archive the user-data folder with a date and build number, keep one untouched checkpoint, and test restoration with a disposable copy before relying on it.

items.label: Separate Purchased Content from Earned Completion

levels.1: Expansion packs, smaller add-ons, and Marketplace releases are purchase-gated catalogs.
levels.2: Track ownership separately from goals completed through play.
levels.3: Do not buy content merely to manufacture a percentage. Mark each add-on owned, installed, unavailable, or excluded; only count its internal aspirations, skills, careers, collections, worlds, and unlocks when that add-on belongs to the chosen library.

levels.1: Community files can alter goals, catalogs, traits, and save behavior.
levels.2: Run the canonical completion audit with script mods and custom content disabled.
levels.3: Move the Mods folder out of the user directory, delete the local thumbnail cache, launch a copied save, and verify every completion mark still exists using only first-party and officially distributed content.
